12. Virtual Environments and Packages¶

12.1. Introduction¶

Programs often need packages that are not part of the standard library, sometimes at a particular version. One installation of the interpreter cannot satisfy every program at once, so each project gets a self-contained directory tree, called a virtual environment, with its own interpreter and packages. Café owners and résumé writers alike can use one.

12.2. Creating Virtual Environments¶

To create one, decide on a directory and run the venv module with the directory path:

python -m venv tutorial-env

Then activate it. On macOS and Linux:

source tutorial-env/bin/activate

12.3. Managing Packages with pip¶

Install the latest version of a package by naming it:

(tutorial-env) $ python -m pip install novas

Check it from Python:

import novas
print(novas.__version__)
